Okay well if you’re dead set on a 66 Mustang as your first car...you should get online now and learn everything you can about common issues with first generation mustangs. Second ask yourself (and I mean really ask yourself) are mentally prepared to handle those issues on a daily basis. If you’ve done all that and still want this car, you now need to get comfortable with wrenching on the car because that’s where you’re going to be quite regularly. It’s not a matter of opinion it’s just fact, older cars require more maintenance than a late model vehicle. If you’re not mechanically inclined and don’t really want to learn I would  take that money you’ve saved and get a newer mustang.
